description: Given the head of a linked list and an integer val, remove all the nodes of the linked list that have Node.val == val, and return the new head.
intuition: Use a dummy node before the head to handle removal of the head uniformly. Walk through the list: if the next node's value matches the target, skip it by updating the pointer; otherwise, advance to the next node.
approach: Use a dummy node before the head. Iterate through the list, skipping nodes with the target value by adjusting the previous node's next pointer.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: head = [1,2,6,3,4,5,6], val = 6

dummy -> 1 -> 2 -> 6 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> null
prev = dummy

prev.next=node(1), val=1 != 6 -> advance prev to node(1)
prev.next=node(2), val=2 != 6 -> advance prev to node(2)
prev.next=node(6), val=6 === 6 -> remove!
  prev.next = node(6).next = node(3)
  list: dummy->1->2->3->4->5->6->null, prev still at node(2)
prev.next=node(3), val=3 != 6 -> advance
prev.next=node(4), val=4 != 6 -> advance
prev.next=node(5), val=5 != 6 -> advance
prev.next=node(6), val=6 === 6 -> remove!
  prev.next = null
  list: dummy->1->2->3->4->5->null
prev.next=null -> loop ends

return dummy.next = node(1)

Output: [1,2,3,4,5]
explanation:
1. Create a dummy node pointing to head.
2. Iterate with prev pointer.
3. If prev.next has the target value, skip it.
4. Otherwise, advance prev.
5. Return dummy.next as the new head.
hints: A dummy node handles the case where head itself needs removal.
Check the next node, not the current node, so you can skip it.
Only advance prev when you do not remove a node.
